questions.q: I want to introduce my partner to my friends early on.
questions.ex: A month into dating, I bring them along to dinner with my friends.

questions.q: I've imagined a confession or proposal down to the place and the exact words.
questions.ex: I once decided I'd say it at the top of the Ferris wheel.

questions.q: After a fight, I first want to sort out what actually caused it.
questions.ex: I go back to the start: "Where did this go wrong?"

questions.q: I like to decide where and when we're going on a date ahead of time.
questions.ex: For a Saturday date, the place and meeting time are set by Wednesday.

questions.q: When I like someone, I only talk about it with one person I trust.
questions.ex: I only share my love life with one close friend.

questions.q: I fall for someone only after we've met and talked many times.
questions.ex: It's less love at first sight and more liking a coworker after many chats.

questions.q: After a fight, I want to make up before figuring out why.
questions.ex: Rather than deciding who was wrong, I'd say "Sorry" and get back to normal.

questions.q: If I spot a shop I like on a date, I want to stop by, even if it changes the plan.
questions.ex: On the way to lunch, we walk into a café we just spotted.

questions.q: When I'm interested in someone, I'm the one who goes up and starts talking.
questions.ex: If I like someone, I'm the one who sends the first message.

questions.q: I love talking with my partner about future dreams and "what if" scenarios.
questions.ex: We talk about "If we lived together, which town would we pick?"

questions.q: When my partner comes to me with a problem, I start thinking of solutions first.
questions.ex: While they vent about work, I say "Why not talk to your boss?"

questions.q: I like to agree early on how often we'll keep in touch and on our ground rules.
questions.ex: Right after we start dating, we agree to text before bed.

questions.q: After a date, I want some time alone.
questions.ex: Even after a fun date, I want to unwind by myself at home.

questions.q: For anniversaries, I'd rather go to our usual place than somewhere special.
questions.ex: Even for our one-year anniversary, our usual BBQ place makes me happy.

questions.q: When my partner comes to me with a problem, I start with "I get it."
questions.ex: When they vent about work, I say "That sounds awful" before any advice.

questions.q: I'd rather decide where to go after we meet up.
questions.ex: We meet first, then figure out together "Where should we go?"

INTJ.name: Owl in Love
INTJ.one: You look up the route before a date.
INTJ.desc: It takes you a while to fall for someone. Before you confess, you go over what to say in your head many times. On date day, you look up the way to the restaurant ahead of time. Your texts are short and only say what's needed, so people often think you're cold. But you start picking anniversary gifts early and take your time choosing.
good: You look up the route before dates
You truly support your partner's dreams
You quickly think of answers when they need advice
care: Your texts only say what's needed
You keep saying what's right in fights
You don't show your jealousy
You plan the future on your own
You don't know when to lean on them
INTJ.tip: In today's text, after the main point, add one line: "I was happy to see you." It helps your feelings come across.
best: INTP
You both need time alone. Even if you spend weekends apart, you can talk on the phone for a long time at night. They add ideas you didn't think of to the plans you make.
hard: ISFJ
They feel safe with a "good morning" every day and small, thoughtful gestures. If you keep sending replies that only say what's needed, they may feel lonely but keep it to themselves.
INTJ.fall: Even when you like someone, you don't act much differently, so people around you rarely notice. Instead, you slowly start making plans to meet, just the two of you. Around the third time, you finally start joking around.
INTJ.date: With your partner, you make jokes you don't make with other people. At home you often lounge on the couch, and they're surprised: "You're so different from usual."
INTJ.fight: You don't raise your voice. You try to go through where things went off track, step by step. They often just want you to listen, but you tend to give them answers. If you say "Tell me everything you want to say first" before you talk, the conversation moves forward.
INTJ.last: For big things like a trip or a move, ask "What do you want to do?" before you decide. Just adding their thoughts makes it feel like you decided together.

INTP.name: Cat in Love
INTP.one: You remember the stories your crush tells.
INTP.desc: You secretly check out the books and movies your crush mentions. Yet somehow, your reply comes the next day. Bookstores and museums make the best dates, and late-night calls never seem to end. When they ask, "What do you like about me?" you think so hard about it that the answer just won't come.
good: You never push plans on them
You think through their worries with them
You don't raise your voice in fights
care: Your replies often come the next day
You tend to forget anniversaries
You explain your reasons step by step mid-fight
"What do you like about me?" stumps you
You keep missing the moment to confess
INTP.tip: When something reminds you of them, send one line right then: "Saw this and thought of you." It's fine even before your thoughts are sorted.
best: INTJ
They plan the date, so you can just enjoy the day. Talking on the way home, you lose track of time.
hard: ISFP
They read feelings from your face and tone of voice. When you go quiet to think, they may worry, "Are you mad?"
INTP.fall: You start talking to them a little more often. But you don't know what to say, so you end up talking only about work or hobbies. Sometimes a friend says, "Don't you like them?" and that's when you realize it.
INTP.date: Once you're comfortable, you talk a lot, but only with your partner. You might send a bunch of news stories and videos you liked all at once at night.
INTP.fight: The words don't come right away, so you go quiet. To them it looks like you're angry, but you're just thinking about what happened. Saying "Give me 30 minutes to think" makes it easier for them to wait.
INTP.last: When you meet, put your phone away and make a little time to talk. Since your replies are slow, talking in person helps them feel secure.

ENTJ.name: Lion in Love
ENTJ.one: You're the one who confesses first.
ENTJ.desc: When you like someone, you're the one who confesses. You book the anniversary dinner early and decide where you'll go that day. If your partner is having a hard time, you listen and then help right away. But your texts tend to stop once the business is done. Even on dates, you end up deciding where to go and in what order.
good: You act fast when they need help
You talk about the future too
Their wins make you as happy as your own
care: Texts end once business is done
You decide everything, even on dates
You set goals even in love
You push for a quick answer in fights
You can't admit you're struggling
ENTJ.tip: For the next date, let your partner choose just one place. They'll be happy you left it to them.
best: ENTP
When you make a plan, they jump in with, "Wouldn't this be more fun?" You two get closer after you argue.
hard: ESFJ
You both want to make the date plans yourselves. You pick what saves time and effort, and they pick what everyone will enjoy, so you tend to clash every time you plan a trip.
ENTJ.fall: When you like someone, you ask them to dinner right away. On the way home from the first date, you've already set the day for the second. Waiting for an answer isn't your strong point.
ENTJ.date: Even in busy weeks at work, you put your dates on the calendar first. When your partner asks for advice about work, you figure out the next step together.
ENTJ.fight: You want to fix it fast, so you try to wrap it up with "Okay, from now on let's do this." But often they haven't calmed down yet. Before you wrap up, just say "Sorry I upset you," and you'll see their face soften.
ENTJ.last: In weeks too busy to meet, try a five-minute call before bed. Even short, when it happens every week, they feel secure.

ENTP.name: Fox in Love
ENTP.one: The more you like someone, the more you tease them.
ENTP.desc: The more you like someone, the more you want to tease them, and even your confession comes out like a joke. You often change plans mid-date with "Actually, let's go there." You're fun to talk to, and you're good at making your partner laugh when they're down. But your replies come fast or slow depending on your mood. When someone chases you, your feelings can suddenly cool.
good: Good at making them laugh when they're down
You get into their stories and keep them going
You don't get mad at different opinions
care: Even your confession sounds like a joke
You suddenly change plans mid-date
Your replies change with your mood
You end up enjoying the argument in fights
Being chased cools you off
ENTP.tip: When your partner starts a serious talk, hold back one joke and just say, "Yeah, and then?"
best: ENTJ
They go ahead and book the trip you mentioned on a whim. Something you said as a joke turns into a real plan.
hard: ESFP
They want to hear "I like you" and take it at face value. Each time you get shy and joke it off, they may feel you're dodging.
ENTP.fall: You start showing up to any drinks they'll be at, as much as you can. When you click, you're so happy that the texts can go on past midnight.
ENTP.date: You want to go places neither of you has been. You pick trips because "we haven't been there yet." When the weekends start to feel the same, you get a little bored.
ENTP.fight: You can't help pointing out where their argument doesn't add up. But they usually want to be understood more than they want to be right. When you want to argue back, first say "So that's how you felt," and the fight won't drag on.
ENTP.last: Pick one thing you've never done together each month and try it. A new restaurant or cooking something new is fine, and you won't get bored.

INFJ.name: Whale in Love
INFJ.one: You notice the smallest changes in your partner right away.
INFJ.desc: You quickly notice a change in your partner's voice or a reply that's a little different from usual. You reread your texts several times before sending. You remember the days that matter to you both, and it makes you a little sad when they forget. But you tend to keep quiet about what you want and hope they'll notice. When you hold it in too long, you may suddenly stop texting.
good: You stay in love for a long time
care: You reread texts over and over before sending
You go quiet, hoping they'll notice
You notice lies quickly
You want a lot from a partner
You suddenly stop texting when you hold in too much
INFJ.tip: When you wish they'd notice, send that feeling in one sentence. Putting it into words gets it across.
best: INFP
On late-night calls, when you start to say something, they wait with "And then?" They don't rush you, so you can talk about things you usually keep to yourself.
hard: ISTJ
They feel safe with the usual place and the usual plan. On nights you want to talk feelings, they may reply, "So, what time tomorrow?" and you end up out of sync.
INFJ.fall: You keep checking their social media again and again. Talking to them first feels a little scary, so when they talk to you, you're happy all day. But it doesn't show much on your face.
INFJ.date: On late-night calls, you slowly start sharing things you don't usually tell people. For dates, you pick a quiet place where you can talk over a busy one.
INFJ.fight: You don't argue back in the moment. You think it over alone after you get home. It can take a few days to sort out how you feel. Before you go quiet, just text "I need a little time to think. Let's talk this weekend," and they won't worry.
INFJ.last: Once a month, share one thing that made you happy lately and one thing that bothered you a little. When it comes with good news, the hard part is easier to say.

INFP.name: Hedgehog in Love
INFP.one: You replay one thing they said, again and again.
INFP.desc: When your crush texts, you leave it on read and spend hours thinking about what to reply. Around them, the words don't come out right, and on the way home you keep thinking, "I should've said that." You're scared of being turned down, so you can't confess first. You hope they'll say it. After a fight, you sometimes cry alone, going over what they said.
good: Your words come from the heart
care: Leaving texts on read for hours
Struggling to talk around your crush
Picturing the future before dating
Hearing every love song as your own
Remembering only your ex's good side
INFP.tip: When you can't decide how to reply, just send one sticker first. You can send the rest later, when you're ready.
best: INFJ
When you can't put a feeling into words, they ask, "You mean like this?" and say it for you. You can talk for hours in a quiet café.
hard: ISTP
They help with actions, like fixing your bike, more than with talk about feelings. On nights you want them to say "I love you," their replies can seem cold.
INFP.fall: A small kind thing they did can make you happy for days. The night before you meet, you can't decide what to wear and can't fall asleep.
INFP.date: Little by little, you pick up pet names and things only the two of you get. Once you feel safe, you get more affectionate than anyone else ever sees.
INFP.fight: Even when you have something to say, the words won't come and you go quiet. Because you couldn't say it, you feel sadder and sadder later. Even in the middle of it, just say, "I'm not angry, I was hurt," and they'll start talking more gently.
INFP.last: If days go by without seeing each other, make a short call before you get lost in your thoughts. Just hearing their voice makes the worry a little smaller.

ENFJ.name: Dolphin in Love
ENFJ.one: You're your partner's biggest fan when it comes to their dreams.
ENFJ.desc: You start planning anniversary surprises weeks ahead. When your partner talks about a dream, you cheer them on like it's your own. Your texts are always thoughtful, and you get along with their family and friends right away. But you don't want them to dislike you, so after a fight you're the one who apologizes first. Later, you sometimes feel bothered: "Why am I always the one saying sorry?"
good: You get along with their family
care: Apologizing first after fights
Always going where they want
Giving them advice too often
Even helping their ex with problems
Expecting something back for what you do
ENFJ.tip: For your next date, name just one place you want to go. It's okay to say, "I'd love to go here with you."
best: ENFP
They're happier than anyone on the dates you plan. You compliment each other, and you're soon talking about your next trip.
hard: ESTJ
They care more about decisions and results than feelings. When you want them to hear how you feel, they ask, "So what are you going to do?" and the conversation doesn't quite click.
ENFJ.fall: Your voice gets a little higher only when you talk to them, so your friends figure it out fast. At first, you invite them to a dinner with other friends too.
ENFJ.date: You remember your partner's schedule, and the night before an interview or a big presentation, you text "Good luck tomorrow." On days off, you look up a place they once said they wanted to go and invite them.
ENFJ.fight: You think so much about their feelings that you forget what you were upset about. You remember what you didn't say only after you get home. Before you apologize, say one thing: "This part bothered me." You'll feel less stuck later.
ENFJ.last: Keep one day a week with no plans for your partner. Having your own time makes it easier to stay kind to them.

ENFP.name: Otter in Love
ENFP.one: Your feelings show on your face right away.
ENFP.desc: You fall for people fast, and your feelings show right away. When something good happens, you send several texts in a row. Where you go on a date is often decided that day, and when you spot a shop that catches your eye, you want to stop in. But if the texts stop for a bit, you get anxious, and jealousy shows on your face right away.
good: You say "I like you" right away
You're always smiling when you meet
You enjoy their dreams with them
You bounce back fast when you're down
care: You send several texts in a row
You get anxious fast when they don't text
Date plans get decided that day
Jealousy shows on your face
You want to run when you feel tied down
ENFP.tip: When you feel anxious, before you send more texts, try saying just one thing: "I'm feeling a little lonely right now."
best: ENFJ
When you say "I want to go there!", they make it a plan right away. With them, your ideas turn straight into trips and dates.
hard: ESTP
They like to enjoy the moment. When you want to talk about the future at night, they brush it off with "Why think that far ahead?" and you can end up feeling lonely.
words: Partner is like a best friend
ENFP.fall: Whatever they like, you try it right away. A song they recommend, you're already playing on the way home. The day after you meet, you're thinking up a reason to ask them out again.
ENFP.date: When something good happens, they're the first person you want to tell. But when you're busy, your texts can suddenly drop off.
ENFP.fight: Sad feelings come out as words, and you say too much. You feel bad right away and text "Sorry about earlier." Taking a sip of water before you answer back helps you say less.
ENFP.last: After you share something happy, ask about their day too. When they feel heard, they'll want to talk more.

ISTJ.name: Beaver in Love
ISTJ.one: You always get there before the meeting time.
ISTJ.desc: On dates, your usual restaurant feels the most comfortable. You always get there 10 minutes early. You're too shy to say sweet things. Instead, you always keep your promises. But if they say on the day, "Let's go somewhere else instead," you don't show it, but you feel a little thrown.
good: You text at the same time daily
No need to worry about cheating
You do what they ask right away
care: Always the same restaurant
Rarely saying "I love you"
Going quiet when plans change
Being slow to apologize after fights
Not good with surprises
ISTJ.tip: On your next date, try one place you've never been. A day that's a little different can become a great memory.
best: ISTP
You plan the weekend, and they add a small detour on a whim. You both talk less, so it never feels awkward when things get quiet.
hard: INFJ
They want to talk slowly about feelings, like "How do you feel about us lately?" When you answer, "We see each other, and I keep my promises," it isn't what they wanted to hear.
ISTJ.fall: Even when you like someone, you don't move fast. You talk a few times, and only once you know you can trust them do you ask them to dinner. When you do, you give a clear day and place.
ISTJ.date: The days and times you meet start to settle into a pattern. Talking early about things like how to split date costs helps you both relax.
ISTJ.fight: You tend to bring up the past: "You said this last time too." Because you remember so well, they feel blamed. Agree to talk only about today, and fights stay short.
ISTJ.last: Now and then, add "Here's what happened today" to your usual texts. It makes them feel closer to you than routine messages alone.

ISFJ.name: Bear in Love
ISFJ.one: You remember the favorite foods of the one you love.
ISFJ.desc: If your partner says their throat hurts, you bring throat drops the next time you meet. You remember their favorite drinks and the foods they don't like, and you have things ready before they ask. "Don't push yourself too hard" is something you text a lot. But even on days you feel lonely, you reply, "I'm fine." Afterward, you sometimes feel down on your own.
good: You notice when they're not feeling well
You put care into home dates
care: Hiding feelings behind "I'm fine"
Putting your own plans last
Not being able to pick a date spot
Holding it in, then suddenly crying
Not being able to throw old things away
ISFJ.tip: Today, when you start typing "I'm fine," add a few words about how you feel. Something like "I missed you" is enough.
best: ISFP
When they suggest a walk or a café on a whim, you're happy to go along. You both dislike fighting, so relaxing at home together is what you enjoy most.
hard: INTJ
They show how they feel by making plans for the future. They don't easily notice the small things you do for them every day. When you don't hear "thank you," you can feel lonely.
ISFJ.fall: You can't easily ask them out yourself. When they ask you, you're so happy you'll move other plans to make time. When a friend says "You seem happy lately," you realize they've figured it out.
ISFJ.date: You try to match your partner's daily rhythm. If they're a night owl, you stay up a bit later to talk on the phone with them.
ISFJ.fight: When an argument starts, you hold back to end it. But you remember what you held back, and later it suddenly spills out. Tell them just one thing you wanted them to do, and it's easier for them to change.
ISFJ.last: Don't hold back from asking them to help around the house. If you cooked, it's fair to ask them to do the dishes.

ESTJ.name: Elephant in Love
ESTJ.one: You set up every detail of the date, all at once.
ESTJ.desc: You set the day and the place for the next date before the day is over. You make the reservations yourself, too. Your texts are short, like "Sat 11am, at the station gate." Things get done fast when you're around, so your partner counts on you a lot. But when they start talking about their feelings after a fight, you rush to the answer: "So, what do you want to do?"
good: You always do what you say
You're clear about whether you're dating
care: You plan things in too much detail
You cut in before they finish
You're strict about being late
You act fine even when you're tired
Romantic stuff makes you shy
ESTJ.tip: Next time they start talking, listen all the way to the end without cutting in. Before you give an answer, just say "Oh, I see" once. That's enough.
best: ESTP
When they say "Let's go now!" you look up the trains and places right away. They come up with the idea and you make the plan, so you can head out that same day.
hard: ENFJ
They want to talk about feelings slowly. When you jump in with "Okay, let's do this," they tend to feel you aren't listening to how they feel.
ESTJ.fall: When you like someone, you don't hide it from people around you. You ask them to dinner early, and after a few dates you want to be clear about whether you're together. You don't like staying in a gray area for long.
ESTJ.date: Once you're together, you introduce them to your family and friends early. You celebrate birthdays and anniversaries properly every year, so they feel secure.
ESTJ.fight: As you talk, your voice tends to get louder. You think you're explaining, but to them it sounds like you're scolding. If they go quiet, don't push. Just stop and say, "Let's talk about it later."
ESTJ.last: Now and then, take a day off with nothing planned. Spend it however you feel, and you'll see a side of them you didn't know.

ESFJ.name: Penguin in Love
ESFJ.desc: You're the type who remembers the day you started dating and your first date. You quickly learn your partner's favorite foods and their friends' names. You start thinking about their birthday gift a month ahead. You reply to texts fast and often check on how they're feeling. But if it feels like you're the only one doing things, you quietly start to wear out.
good: You get ready for birthdays early
You quickly get along with their friends
care: You go along with them until you're tired
You notice when there's no thank-you
You want to know their plans
You hold in complaints, then say them all at once
You care how others see you
ESFJ.tip: Today, ask them for one thing: "Next time, could you do this for me?" Getting used to letting them do things for you helps you not wear out.
best: ESFP
When they say, "I want to go here," you make the plan. Their ideas and your planning fit together, so you naturally go out together more often.
hard: ENTJ
You both want to make the plans yourselves. You choose by whether they'll be happy, and they choose by time and effort, so you tend to clash every time you plan a trip.
ESFJ.fall: When you start liking someone, you tell a close friend right away and figure out together how to ask them out. Before you ask, you look up a few places they'd probably like and pick one.
ESFJ.date: You want to make little rules for the two of you, like "text good night before bed" or "eat at home once a month." Having them set makes you feel at ease.
ESFJ.fight: In the moment, you tend to smile and say "It's fine." Then on another day, something small sets you off, and you bring up old things too. Before you say "It's fine," try saying "Let me think about it." That gives you time to think about how you feel.
ESFJ.last: Talk with your partner once about whether to post photos of the two of you on social media. If you care about different things, it can lead to small misunderstandings.

ISTP.name: Wolf in Love
ISTP.one: You don't say "I love you," but you quietly help.
ISTP.desc: When your partner is having trouble, you come over to help without saying a word. You can quickly fix a flat bike tire or put furniture together. Your replies are often just one emoji. You don't try to tie them down, so they say you're easy to be with. But when they ask, "How do you feel about me?" you can't find the words and go quiet.
good: You quietly help when they need it
Easy to be with, never controlling
care: Your texts end with just an emoji
You hardly ever say "I love you"
You get quiet without alone time
You go silent when feelings come up
You let them pick where to go on dates
ISTP.tip: Today, after you help them with something, add just one line: "Because I love you." When they know why, they feel reassured.
best: ISTJ
You can follow the date plans they make without worry. Neither of you talks much, so it's not awkward even when a drive is quiet.
hard: INFP
They want to talk about feelings, slowly and in words. Your short "Eh, it's fine" can sound like you don't care about their feelings.
ISTP.fall: You hardly say it in words. Instead, you casually invite them to a place they said they wanted to go. Then you notice you're replying faster to their texts than anyone else's.
ISTP.date: You don't really text each other every day. When you meet, you have fun, and on other days you each do your own hobbies. Even if they feel lonely, you may not notice until they tell you.
ISTP.fight: When an argument drags on, you want to leave. As you leave the room, just say "I'm going to cool off. I'll be back in an hour," and they won't feel left behind.
ISTP.last: Once a month, pick the date spot yourself and ask them out. The fact that you thought about it makes them happy.

ISFP.name: Panda in Love
ISFP.one: You remember the views you saw together, forever.
ISFP.desc: Your date plans are loose, and you like stepping into any café that catches your eye. Instead of saying "I like you," you find a little something that would suit them and give it to them. When a fight seems close, you tend to laugh and change the subject. When something bothers you, your replies slowly get later.
good: You send them photos of pretty views
care: Tight schedules wear you out
You go quiet in fights
When upset, you reply slowly
You put off talk about the future
Wanting to meet depends on your mood
ISFP.tip: When something bothers you, say one thing about it that same day. Something short like "That bugged me a little" is fine.
best: ISFJ
When you say, "Let's go into this café," they happily come along. Neither of you likes arguing, so your time together stays calm.
hard: INTP
They like to find a reason, even for feelings. When you say, "I just didn't like it," they ask, "Why?" You can't really answer, and it wears you out.
ISFP.fall: Some days you suddenly really want to see them. You might text out of nowhere, "Can we meet for a bit now?" But saying "I like you" out loud feels too embarrassing.
ISFP.date: Your favorite days are cooking together at home or napping together. A free day off spent relaxing together is all you need.
ISFP.fight: The words don't come quickly, so you say, "It's fine." But your feelings don't go back to normal for a while. Talking while you take a walk is easier than sitting face to face.
ISFP.last: Start future talk with near plans, like "Where should we go next summer?" Starting close makes it easier to think further ahead.

ESTP.name: Cheetah in Love
ESTP.tag: Asks You Out on the Spot
ESTP.one: You're the first to send "Free today?"
ESTP.desc: When you like someone, you text "Want to get dinner today?" before you have time to hesitate. On weekends you often just head out to wherever comes to mind, so time with you is never boring. You don't hold on to small things, so the day after a fight you're back to normal. But when the talk turns to "Where is this going?" your replies suddenly get short.
good: You head out the moment an idea hits
You don't carry fights into the next day
You come right over when they call
You show them new ways to have fun
care: You get close too fast
You change the subject when things get heavy
You stop replying when you get bored
Future plans are mostly undecided
You forget promises made in the moment
ESTP.tip: On the way home from a fun date, ask just one thing: "How was today?" Knowing how they felt makes the next date even more fun.
best: ESTJ
When you say, "Let's go somewhere," they decide where to go and even when to head home. Your idea turns into a real date, just like that.
hard: ENFP
They want to talk slowly about their dreams and your future together. When you answer, "As long as we're having fun now," they tend to feel you aren't taking the two of you seriously.
ESTP.fall: You quickly invite them to play the sport or game they like: "Let's do it together." When you're with them, you naturally end up close to them.
ESTP.date: Even in a relationship, your pace doesn't change much. In weeks full of work or fun, you may see each other less. But on days you decide to meet, you make sure they have a good time.
ESTP.fight: You want it over fast, so you say "Let's just drop it." You think you let it go, but their feelings are still there. Before you end it, ask once, "What bothered you most?" and the same fight is less likely to come back.
ESTP.last: When you make a promise, put it in your phone's calendar right then. Just keeping the promises you made in the moment makes them trust you more.

ESFP.name: Parakeet in Love
ESFP.one: You bring a small surprise every time you meet.
ESFP.desc: When you fall for someone, you go all in. On days you meet, you bring a small surprise. Your phone fills up with photos after every date, and on the way home you text right away: "Today was so fun!" You show your love in both words and actions, so your partner feels cared for. But if a reply is a little late, you start to worry: "Are they losing interest?"
good: You text as soon as you get home
You notice a new haircut right away
Being with you lifts their mood
care: Slow replies make you worry
You pack in too many plans
You laugh fights off
You go quiet when the future comes up
Days apart feel really lonely
ESFP.tip: Tonight, spend an evening doing nothing with them. Once you can enjoy quiet time too, it gets easier to stay together for a long time.
best: ESFJ
They remember the dates you enjoyed as special days. You come up with fun plans and they treasure them, so it tends to last.
hard: ENTP
They enjoy playful arguing and mind games, even with a partner. When you say, "I was lonely," and they answer with logic, you can end up feeling alone.
ESFP.fall: You tell your friends right away: "I like someone!" On days you meet, you spend extra time on your clothes and hair.
ESFP.date: You keep finding more things you want to do with your partner. Whether it's fireworks or a concert, just going together is fun. On days apart, you call and tell them all about your day.
ESFP.fight: You don't want things to feel heavy, so you crack a joke. But they want to talk seriously, so it can make them angrier. When you feel like laughing, nod once and listen to the end. The fight will end sooner.
ESFP.last: On days you can't meet, plan one thing with friends or something you enjoy. You'll spend less time feeling lonely and anxious.
